prerequisites.text: All members of the cluster must be at least version 3.2. The upgrade process warns about any component running an earlier version.

steps.text: Disable the balancer as described in Disable the Balancer.

Wait for the member to recover to SECONDARY state (check with rs.status()) before upgrading the next secondary.
Connect to the primary and run rs.stepDown() to force an election.
When rs.status() shows another member is PRIMARY, shut down the stepped-down primary, replace the binary with 3.4, and start it with the same options.

steps.text: Upgrade all config server replica set instances first, then all shard members, and finally the mongos instances; upgrading mongos earlier can cause compatibility issues. Replace each mongos instance with the 9.0 binary and restart it, including any other configuration for your deployment. --bind_ip must be specified when members run on different hosts or remote clients connect.
Using mongosh, connect to a mongos and run sh.startBalancer().

On a mongos, run setFeatureCompatibilityVersion in the admin database to enable the 9.0 features. You must also set confirm to true. It implicitly runs replSetReconfig on each shard to add the term field and does not complete until the configuration propagates to a majority. The command is idempotent and safe to retry on the mongos. When the FCV is upgraded to 9.0, MongoDB migrates metadata from the config server to the shards (one-time, can take longer with many databases, collections or chunks). Operations that modify, rename, reshard or drop a database/collection wait while its metadata is cloned; split, mergeChunks, mergeAllChunksOnShard and migrations are drained and blocked until the FCV upgrade completes; movePrimary fails with ConflictingOperationInProgress and should be retried afterwards. Note: a 8.3 mongos cannot connect to mongod instances once the FCV is 9.0. The doc tip: enabling these features can complicate a downgrade, so it recommends a burn-in period without them until the likelihood of downgrade is minimal.
